market_size: Moderate local demand with approximately 150 monthly searches on the primary keyword. Winnebago County contains roughly 115,000 housing units, the majority built before 1985 with galvanized sheet metal ductwork that requires periodic cleaning. The market covers Rockford proper plus 10 surrounding communities across Winnebago, Boone, and Ogle counties, creating an addressable pool of 60,000 to 80,000 single-family and multi-unit homes likely to need service within a 5-year cycle.

peak: September through November — homeowners activate furnaces before northern Illinois winters and book duct cleaning before first frost. Highest call volume of the year.
March through May — spring allergen season drives demand as ragweed and tree pollen from the Rock River valley concentrate inside return air plenums.
Post-renovation surges year-round when homeowners complete remodeling projects involving drywall, tile, or hardwood flooring.
slow: June and July — lowest demand. Heating systems idle. Focus shifts to dryer vent cleaning and commercial HVAC servicing.
January and February — weather deters discretionary spending; primary calls are reactive complaints about poor furnace airflow or burning dust smells.

avg_customer_value: Typical residential job ranges from three hundred to seven hundred dollars for a complete supply, return, and trunk line cleaning on a fifteen to thirty vent home. Add-on services — dryer vent cleaning, sanitization fogging, evaporator coil cleaning — increase average ticket. Dryer vent cleaning alone adds approximately seventy to ninety dollars. Commercial HVAC duct cleaning jobs for retail or office space run higher. Lead rental value to a local contractor is meaningful given repeat-service potential every two to three years.
demand_trigger_events: First furnace activation of autumn producing burning dust smell or musty odor
Moving into a pre-1985 home with previous pet owners or smokers
Post-renovation debris from drywall sanding, tile cutting, or hardwood refinishing pulled into return vents
Allergy or asthma symptom spike correlated with running the HVAC system
Visible black streaks around supply registers or unexplained heavy dust on furniture
Dryer taking two or more cycles to fully dry a load of laundry
Rodent or insect activity suspected in ductwork
Home inspection report flagging dirty or contaminated ductwork
common_pain_points: Bait-and-switch scam: low-price coupon mailers and Facebook ads advertising whole-house cleaning for under one hundred dollars, then manufacturing a toxic mold scare on-site to upsell thousands in unnecessary chemical treatments
Blow-and-go contractors using portable shop vacuums that redistribute dust rather than remove it under negative pressure
Uncertified operators falsely claiming NADCA certification; homeowners have no quick way to verify credentials on-site
Aggressive on-site upselling of ozone generators, UV light installations, and chemical fogging that cost more than the original service without documented mold testing
Physical damage to property — scratched hardwood floors, punctured flexible ductwork, access holes drilled through drywall without proper patching
No before-and-after documentation; homeowners cannot verify work was actually performed inside the trunk lines
Dryer vent fire hazard ignored by general HVAC contractors who only service forced-air ducts
Persistent sinus congestion and dust accumulation on furniture after service due to incomplete cleaning of blower compartment and evaporator coil
